articleTitle: High Frequency Harmonic Input Impedance of an Antenna Embedded in a Conducting Half-Space
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper presents theorical and experimental approach of the harmonic input impedance of a ground connection over a wide range frequency. Transmission line theory, which is first applied to a ground rod, allow an easy definition of grounding impedance but needs several restrictive approximations. Antenna theory does not require these, but is shown that the method of moments which is classicaly applied to antenna problems does not lead directly to the physical grounding impedance. Experimental results, obtained for a hemisphere, a vertical rod and a horizontal wire show that the grounding harmonic impedance strongly depends on the grounding connection geometry.

articleTitle: Rationale and New Experimental Evidence on the Adequacy of Conducted Instead of Radiated Susceptibility Tests
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The synthetic test method (SM) is a conducted susceptibility test for devices with cables. The SM attemps to reproduce those dominant currents which are induced on the device when the device and its cables are exposed to the test field. The theoretical rationale is given for the SM and comparative test results on 16 TV-receivers up to 225 MHz are presented for the SM and for three radiated test methods. The SM gives excellent correlation to radiated methods, the absolute relation between them is approximately predicted. The SM adequately replaces radiated tests up to frequencies, where the dimensions of the device approach λ/2.

articleTitle: Spike Generator - Peak Voltage Detector: A Test System
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper presents a number of applications for an interference test system, consisting of a spike generator and a peak voltage detector. The peak voltage detector has proved to be a convenient replacement for a storage oscilloscope, which would normally be used to detect interference spikes in a system. The specifications of the two instruments are given and tests on a range of mains filters, a noise isolation transformer and ground planes are described. The usefulness of such a test system has mainly been found in performing in situ tests, where only the residual peak voltage is sufficient to indicate whether the components provided for obtaining electromagnetic compatibility were correctly chosen and installed.

articleTitle: Effective Frequency Spectrum Utilization using an Algorithm for Automated Channel Allocation in Land Mobile Service
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Principles of detailed EMC analysis in land mobile service are presented, and two algorithms for automated channel allocation to land mobile networks using quasi-optimal frequency planning techniques are described. The first algorithm is intended for long-term territorial frequency planning, and the second one for operational frequency allocation to a land mobile network which is not foreseen by the frequency plan. Use of these algorithms enhances the effectivity of allotted spectrum utilization.

articleTitle: Pulse Spectrum Density Errors and Mitigation
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In EMI calculations of conducted and radiated emission levels from transients and pulses, it is common practice to employ the envelope approximation to the classical sin(x)/x pulse spectral-density function. While convenience of its simple envelope formatting appears to justify the approximation, adjustments in its pessimistic errors (predicted EMI is on the high side) are rarely made. This article shows that for conducted baseband situations, these errors range from about 2 dB for triangular shaped transients to 17 dB for pulses having a pulse-duration- to-rise-time-ratio of 100. Typical computer clocks (ratio of about 5-10) exhibit errors of about 8 dB. The article shows that when one or more numerical convolutions is performed to produce crosstalk, radiated emissions or pick up, and bandwidth limiting, prediction errors can also be quantified and corrected. When the victim is a receiver, and its lower cutoff frequency exists above the second corner frequency of the pulse and its bandwidth is much greater than the reciprocal of the pulse width, then errors in using the sin(x)/x envelope approximation can become arbitrarily great. The article concludes with suggestions on how to modify the envelope of the classical sin(x)/x pulse spectral-density function to reduce errors to acceptable levels.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>

articleTitle: Review of Hybrid and Equivalent-Electric-Dipole EMP Simulators
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper summarizes the design principles for two important classes of simulators for the high-altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse (EMP). First there is the equivalent electric dipole in the form of a resistively loaded cone on a ground plane; this is appropriate for radiating an optimum pulse to distances large compared to the simulator; it can also expose systems on the ground to a vertically polarized electric field. Second there is a hybrid type of EMP simulator which is appropriate for producing an approximate plane wave incident on systems on the ground surface together with the ground reflected wave.

articleTitle: EMI in Microelectronics-an Update
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The status of determining EMI in microelectronics is updated. The investigations reviewed continue to emphasize how single or pairs of integrated circuits (ICs) respond to conducted EMI signals which are injected onto leads connected to the IC pins. The review considers EMI in both analog and digital ICs. Comparisons of EMI in ICs and statistical approaches for EMI in ICs are also reviewed.

articleTitle: Probability Distibution of Time Intervals between Pulses of VLF Atmospheric Noise
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A model of probability distribution of time intervals between atmospheric noise pulses in the frequency band 3+30 kHz is proposed in order to describe the appropriate experimental data. The model is based on the presentation of the sequence of pulses as a poisson sequence of groups with poisson intergroup structure having the pulse intensity rate within groups changing according to exponential law. The analysis of the model is completed by deriving expressions for probability distributions of time intervals between arbitrary time moment and the ajacent pulse as well as between pairs of ajacent pulses. Using the experimental data the model parameters are specified, their values being in agreement with known physical properties of VLF radio noise.

articleTitle: Target Interactions and Influence of Grouding Electrodes in an EMP Simulator
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A frequent way to simulate the interaction between an EMP plane and a target it to use a guiding structure to create, in the neighbourhood of the target, an electromagnetic field similar to the EMP field. Differences between the real case and the simulated one can occur for differents reasons. Two of them are: - interaction between target and simulator - behaviour of grounding electrodes. This paper deals with these problems.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Measuring and Control Circuits in High-Power Test Laboratories
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: There are reported the particular difficulties arising when electronic measuring and control equipment is used in a high-power test laboratory. On the basis of the experience gathered during various tests and with different test arrangements, there is described an earthing and protection system where, despite extreme conditions caused by strong electric and magnetic fields, disturbance of the acquisition, transmission and processing of the signals is avoided. High-resolution oscillograms of several tests are shown.

articleTitle: RFI Effects in Mosfet Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Digital integrated circuits, microprocessors in particular, are being used in a wide variety of applications. Many of these applications were previously the domain of analog circuitry. In a number of these applications there exists the possibility for the introduction of radio frequency interference (RFI) into the circuitry. In some cases, because of the make-up of the analog circuit, RFI could be tolerated with no ill effect. This, however, may not be the case for digital circuits. Since many digital circuits are fabricated as MOSFET integrated circuits, an investigation has been undertaken to determine the susceptibility of a MOSFET IC to being "upset" by the effects of RFI.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Casings for Interference Fields Caused by Lightning Strokes
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The lightning stroke into a building causes strong pulse shaped magnetic fields in the surrounding of the rods in consequence to the lightning current To avoid induction effects in sensitive electronic circuits shielding is applied. In laboratory the shielding effectiveness was investigated considering the special conditions of lightning discharge. The present paper encloses a brief description of test arrangement, measuring method, description and interpretation of results.

articleTitle: The HF Properties of RFI Suppression Chokes With Soft Magnetic Tape-Wound Cores as Compared with Ferrite Cores
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Current compensated RFI suppression chokes are used to suppress interference in equipments which produce high frequency interference in the range 10 kHz to 30 MHz. If these chokes are to operate effectively at low frequencies inductance values of several mH are required at a measurement frequency of 10 kHz. The frequency characteristics of conventional current compensated chokes with ferrite toroidal cores then exhibits the well known curve characterized by several maxima and minima. A comparison of the above frequency characteristics with that of a current compensated choke with a high permeable toroidal tape-wound core of identical dimensions shows that the frequency characteristics of this choke exhibits a constant level of attenuation without maximum and minimum resonance peaks. Moreover, a comparison of calculations with measurements shows that the eddy currents in the toroidal tape cores are the main cause of this behaviour.

articleTitle: The Pulse Power Technology of High Altitude EMP Simulators
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Guided-wave, hybrid and radiating (or equivalent-electric dipole) are three classes of HAEMP simulator that require similar pulse generators. They all present -100 ohms impedance to the pulser at early times, though they have different impedance-time characteristics later in the pulse. Marx generators are used to drive the simulators with voltages of many megavolts. To obtain fast risetimes, low inductance pulse capacitors (peaking or transfer) are added to the Marx, and low inductance pressurised SF5 output switches are used. With the correct choice of pulse capacitor dielectric and configuration, the pulse capacitor does not greatly disturb the wave launched on the simulator. Output switches have low nanosecond jitter in self-breaking mode, allowing synchronisation of modules; triggered versions could produce shorter risetimes than the lns/MV typical of single channels. Choice of pulser insulation - usually gas or oil - is often determined by weight constraints.

articleTitle: EMC Aspects of Phased Array Radar Design
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The high-performance AN/SPY-1A phased array radar, developed for the AEGIS Weapon System, is capable of automatically detecting, tracking, and engaging large numbers of aircraft and missiles while maintaining continuous hemispheric air surveillance. Achievement of these performance standards in the adverse ship- board/fleet electromagnatic environment required the integration of electromagnetic compatibility control features in the radar design. EMC techniques integrated into the AN/SPY-1A design are described and shown to be readily adaptable to the design of other radar systems.

articleTitle: Linear Antenna Near-Field Decoupling using A Radial Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A method has been demonstrated to reduce the EMC problems associated with near-field coupling between a monopole or stub-type transmitting antenna and other antennas or electronic assemblies in the immediate vicinity. The technique involves use of a radial-transmission-line equivalent of a λ/4 choke mounted at the base of the monopole or stub antenna (concentric with the antenna-feed coaxial line) to provide decoupling of the inductive fields of the antenna from nearby conductive elements. As a result of the phase shift in the radially-traveling waves, produced by a very small inner radius, the radial-transmission- line choke can provide for a structure smaller in size and much more readily adaptable to installation on aircraft, small ships or land vehicles than a conventional λ/4 coaxial-line choke.

articleTitle: Forthcoming American National Standards: New Documents and Revisions to Old Ones
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper brings the world—wide community of Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) scientists , engineers, and technical workers up to date on forthcoming American National Standards on EMC. The documents covered include not only wholly new EMC standards, but forthcoming revisions to old EMC standards as well. The many standards writing bodies in the United States of America are introduced, the thrusts of their efforts as they concern EMC are mentioned, and their interrelationships are explained. The new and revised documents that are in progress are discussed in some detail so that the readers may understand the direction that EMC standards efforts are taking in the U.S.A.

articleTitle: An Investigation into the Screening Performance of Aircraft Access Panels and Doors
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The work reported in this paper was initiated in order to compare the electromagnetic (E.M.) shielding performance, of hinged, quick release access doors and bolted access panels manufactured in carbon fibre composite (C.F.C) with identical structures manufactured traditionally in aluminium alloy. The experiment was designed such that aperture coupling around the door or panel edge and diffusion coupling through the door or panel material were the only two mechanisms investigated. The experiment was carried out in a shielded room using computer control of the instrumentation and data collection. Results were "smoothed" in order to remove the resonance effects of the shielded enclosure, this made differences between various results clearer. The electric field shielding performance was measured over the frequency band of 50-100MHz The performance of bolted panels was demonstrated to be adequate in the case of metal or C.F.C., with the exception of C.F.C. / honeycomb sandwich panels. Quick release access door performance, however, in the cases of both C.F.C. and metal was inadequate and design changes would be required to improve electrical contact to the surrounding structure around the periphery of the door. In addition, metallisation of the inner or outer surface is required. The magnetic shielding results obtained over a frequency band of 1-250 MHz demonstrated that only metallised C.F.C. and metal bolted panels exhibit sufficient shielding performance. C.F.C./honeycomb/C.F.C sandwich panels with either an aluminium or nomex honeycomb had a particularly poor magnetic shielding performance. Quick release access doors of all types were shown to have very poor magnetic shielding performance due to the electrically insulating weather seal.

articleTitle: The EMC Figure of Merit in the Prediction of Receptor Compatibility
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: With the EMC figure of merit it is possible to predict quantitatively electromagnetic compatibility or incompatibility of the receptor in the unique way if the receptor performances can be characterized in terms of average power. This paper describes a method of calculating the EMC figure of merit. In the second part an example is given of experimental determination of the receptor compatibility. The receptor used was an impulse generator of three-pulse converter.

articleTitle: Active Broadband Antennas in the 10 kHz to 30 MHz Range
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A survey is presented of the various configurations of small active broadband antennas for measurement of electric or magnetic fields in the frequency range 10 kHz - 30 MHz. The configurations are compared on basis of the minimum field-strength needed to obtain a signal-to-noise ratio equal to one. Special attention is paid to a loop antenna configuration for near-field measurements.

articleTitle: EMC Standards and Their Application in European Countries
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Standards are used all over the world to describe in a unique way procedures, systems or equipment to be applied and supported by manufacturers, users and other interested bodies.

articleTitle: A Procedure for Estimating the Risk of Interference
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A procedure is developed on a probabilistic basis to quantify the risk involved in not achieving an acceptable degree of electromagnetic compatibility. Also developed is a procedure to calculate the direct cost involved in decreasing risk by any given extent. These relationships aid the technical management of an EMC program. They are considered candidates for an EMC standard so that competitive bidders may arrive at numerical values using the same basis for calculation.

articleTitle: Improvements in the Analytical Treatment of Source Region EMP
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A method for rapidly computing the Electro-Magnetic Pulse (EMP) near a nuclear burst at the surface of the earth has been developed by the authors. The present work expands upon earlier work by Crevier and Pettus to include the effects of finite soil conductivity and the self consistent turning of Compton electrons by the EMP. The basic formalism of the previous work is briefly reviewed. Physically based arguments for how to include the effects of finite soil conductivity and turning of the Compton current are presented. Comparisons between the fast analytic code, MODELC, and a more exact two-dimensional finite difference code show that the improvements allow MODELC to rapidly compute source region EMP fields to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> seconds with accuracy sufficient for most applications.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experimental Study of EMP Propagation under the Ground
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: EMP propagation beneath the level of the ground, has been studied both theoretically and experimentally, down to 500 meters depth.

articleTitle: Penetration through an Interruption of the Shield of a Coaxial Cable
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Transmission lines interconnecting electronic equipments are usually surrounded by a shield. If such a cable is situated in a disturbing environment, both common and differential mode coupling occur. The differential voltage, i. e, the induced voltage appearing between two lines disturbs the response of the equipment but the common-mode voltage has a much higher amplitude and can destroy the input stage. In the following, we describe only this effect and thus, to simplify the calculation and the experimentation, we assume that all the inner conductors behave as a single one. Such a cable can be modelled as a coaxial cable. For various reasons, some faults can appear in the shielding continuity, the extreme case being an interruption of the outer shield and there is a coupling of electromagnetic energy through the aperture from the exterior region to the interior region of the cable.

articleTitle: Crosstalk in Digital Systems
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The Fast-crosstalk (FX) behaviour of digital systems is analysed, by means of the 3 conductor system as transmission line (TL) model, in the case of nonlinear digital ICs of the families TTL, ECL and C-MOS. Maximum FX amplitudes are numericaly determined with a computer routine as function of the even- and odd-mode impedances (Zeven and Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">odd</inf>) of the TL-system. The term "dangerous" crosstalk is introduced to specify the regions in the (Zeven, Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">odd</inf>)-plane, for which the FX amplitude exceeds the static noise margins of the specific ICs and consequently may lead to logic errors. Latter results are applied to determine the minimum line-spacings in the case of coupled microstrip and two wires above ground TL-systems, in order to reduce FX to within a tolerable level.

articleTitle: Improvement of Electromagnetic Compatibility by using Interference Cancellers
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The paper discusses problems of interference cancellers utilization for better efficiency of the radio spectrum use by radio relay and satellite communication systems. Results of calculations are given which show that noise cancellers are efficient means allowing to reduce angular or geographical separation between systems experiencing mutual interference. Geostationary orbit capacity limit to be achieved by using noise cancellers in satellite systems is estimated.

articleTitle: Electric Field Measurements over a Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The imposition of FCC Regulation Part 15 Subpart J has generated renewed interest in measuring E fields over a conducting ground plane, which is required by this regulation. This paper presents a tutorial approach to the calculation and measurement of E fields over a ground plane.

articleTitle: EMI Transient Susceptibility OP DC Power Distribution Networks: Prediction Analysis in Time or Frequency Domin
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In designing, field testing and maintening the new electronic switching exchange, as well data processing systems, it has become apparent that the functional structure of the plant must be compatible with a defined architecture, E.M.C. oriented. In the course of the development of the above mentioned systems, transient noises on the DC power buses have been shown to be of particular relevance, in so much as the power distribution system, using switching mode (SW) DC/DC converters on printed board (P.C.B.)level, and the susceptibility of integrated circuits, impose a well known filter behaviour of power supplies to broad band (B.B.)in- put noises. In this paper, the method adopted for integral calculus of spectrum transforms, is outlined. The peak value of time domain transients is then predieted from; modulus of B.B. spectrum transform. The error, due to loss of phase information, is estimated.

articleTitle: A New Method for Determining the Emission Characteristics of an Unknown Interference Source
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Quantitative determination of the radiation characteristics of an unknown interference source is of importance to the users, manufacturers, and regulatory authorities. The theoretical background and measurement procedures for a new method to achieve this objective are presented with experimental results.

articleTitle: Charge Neutralization Problem for a Space Shuttle
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In recent years, artificial electron beams have been injected from rockets and satellites into space to probe the ionosphere and magnetosphere. Then, the charging of the vehicle body to a high positive potential has been observed, thus preventing the beam from escaping to infinity. For the case of Space Shuttle, this problem becomes more severe than for the case of metallic spacecrafts, since Space shuttle is covered with thermal insulation layers, the so-called "tile" over an area of more than 90 % of its surface. This paper presents a means to Shuttle charge neutralization by producing anomalous ionization in the vicity of the body. Two methods are applied, i.e., beam plasma discharge by RF beam pulsation and application of the critical ionization velocity concept by neutral and plasma beam injection into space. Both are expected to enhance ionization and consequently electron return currents that neutralize the Shuttle body through partially exposed conductors such as a pallet area. The methods will be used to the AMPS (Atmosphere, Magnetosphere and Plasma in Space) experiments for the first Spacelab mission to be launched in 1983.

articleTitle: Control of Interference Produced by Motor Vehicles in Road Traffic
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The paper gives a comparative analysis of three methods of radio interference control, which are simpler than the standard method and which can be used in planned periodical inspection of motor vehicles that are in use. Earlier, different authors [1], [2], [3], [4] expressed an idea of using these or similar methods for a periodic control. However, the materials presented by these authors do not enable to compare these methods and to assess the reliability of results obtained in the frequency range 30 to 1000 MHz. As the main parameters of the methods, the coefficients of correlation between the results obtained by simplified methods and by the standard method are considered, as well as the operating-and-technical characteristics of the methods. The reliability of the results being obtained is assessed by two parameters, namely, by a probability of acceptance of a "defective” motor vehicle and by a probability of rejection of an "acceptable" motor vehicle.

articleTitle: Effect of Interference Sources on Receptors
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: With limited information about electromagnetic environment in which a receptor is supposed to be used, the test effects are determined that should be employed when checking a receptor for immunity.

articleTitle: Pulse-Time Modulated Converters for Minimum Harmonic Content and Ideal Power Factor
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The widespread use of phase control in power electronics - as desired by users - until now is strictly limited by regulation. This is due to the decrease in power factor and the increase in harmonic contents due to phase control. A new approach, the so-called pulse-time control (a special case of pulse width modulation, PWM), optimizes power factor and harmonics contents. This is achieved by a combination of line commutation and forced commutation. A computer program has been developed for determination of the proper switching times for line and forced commutation to achieve this objective. A practical system has been built up based upon the computer results. The measurements obtained show that the limits set by standard ΕΝ 50.006 can be met easily. The approach should gain increased interest in the near future. This is due to the already widespread (economic) availability of high power transistors which simplify forced commutation very much.

articleTitle: Sensing of Noise Current Distribution on an Automobile Body Surface
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The surface current of a sedan is measured by using a vector current sensor. The strong noise currents are observed in the neighborhood of the slit between bonnet and fender, and produce horizontally polarized radiations. On the roof, door and trunk, the noise currents are much less.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Multimode Time-Varying Enclosures
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In order to assess the degree of randomization of the microwave field inside a mode-stir red cavity systematic measurements of power reflection and transmission coefficients were carried out, investigating the influence of the radiation frequency (in the 5.5 ÷ 18 GHz range), and of position and polarization of the feeding aperture. The results of more unconventional tests, based on VSWR measurements and on the evaluation of the power absorbed by a probing sample, are also reported, and it is shown that such techniques can give useful information on the behaviour of the cavity expecially in view of some particular applications like the exposure of samples in bioelectromagnetic research and the related dosimetry.

articleTitle: Excitation of a Shielded Multiconductor Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: One problem of current interest in the application of transmission line theory to EMC problems is that of the excitation of shielded multiconductor cables by currents and charges flowing on the exterior of the shield. Previous studies have discussed the excitation of open multiconductor cables by an external electromagnetic field [Ref. 1], and the excitation of a single conductor inside a braided shield has been discussed in Ref, [2] and [3], The purpose of this paper is to outline the steps by which the internal excitation of a shielded multiconductor cable can be determined.

articleTitle: Solution of EMC Problems in a Local Radio-Relay Communications Network with a Ring Structure
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A comparative analysis of star and loop structures of digital radio relay links (DRRL) was performed, which was based on determination of conditions that ensure the EMC, It is shown that loop structures enable to improve electromagnetic environment in the service area of radio facilities and to construct denser networks.

articleTitle: New Guidelines for Radiofrequency Radiation Safety
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Research conducted over the past few years provides a better scientific basis for new radiofrequency radiation (RFR) safety guidelines. This is apparent in recent actions taken by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI), the American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists (ACGIH), and the International Radiation Protection Association (IRPA). The new safety guidelines covering that portion of the electromagnetic spectrum from 10 kHz to 300 GHz limit human exposures to an average whole-body specific absorption rate (SAR) of 0.4 W/kg or less while the average incident power, densities may vary from 1 to 100 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. These limits are based on what is known about the frequency-dependent nature of RFR energy deposition in biological systems and the current knowledge of biological effects. In general, the new guidelines provide an added margin of safety over what was previously used.

articleTitle: Studies of Pulse Interference Effects on a FM Multichannel Troposcatter Communication System
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: With the outside source interference effect on the multi-channel communication system the allowable increase in the level of crosstalk P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">IN</inf> in the worst telephone channel is the main criterium for the possibility of a successful operation of the troposcatter system. Pulse interference effects on P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">IN</inf> for links using PM and trans-horizon troposcatter propagation with due account to diversed reception of fading signals are discussed below. Interference spectra, distribution laws of noise-to-signal ratio at the frequency detector input and simultaneous and mean per minute noise power in telephone channels were obtained in the result of studies. This investigation allows grounding COIR Recommendation on noise power increase in telephone channels under the effect of the outside interference on the troposcatter radio relay links.

articleTitle: A Logical Structure with High Noise Immunity
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In this paper, a logical structure which acts as a gate with variable input voltage and a high output voltage is presented. Its noise voltages are much greater than those of usual gates, so that it may operate in high noise environments. An example illustrates the presentation.

articleTitle: A Comparison of RFI in Operational Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: An experimental investigation has been conducted to determine the statistical variations of RFI demodulation effects in operational amplifiers (op amps). Amplitude-modulated (AM) RF signals were injected into the non-inverting input of an op amp voltage follower circuit to produce undesired demodulated responses at the AM-modulation frequency (1 kHz). The RF frequency was varied over the range 0.1 to 400 MHz. The op amps investigated were the 741 bipolar op amp which has conventional npn input transistors, the LM10 bipolar op amp which has less conventional pnp input transistors, the LF355 JFET-bipolar op amp which has JFET input transistors, and the CA081 M0S- bipolar op amp which has MOSFET input transistors. Ten units of each type were tested. Mean values and standard deviations were determined for demodulation RFI. In the frequency range 1 to 20 MHz where the demodulation RFI effects were largest, the mean values are 10 to 20 dB lower for FET-bipolar op amps than for bipolar op amps.

articleTitle: Impact of Lightning Beams on a Tall Structure
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The studies of lightning to the tall standing structure are not only important to understand lightning characteristics of the transmission line tower, the communication tower and tower for bridge etc., but are also important to understand the effect of tall standing structures on local lightning climatology. The lightning studies using the worlds' highest free standing structure, the CN Communications Tower (553 m AGL), in Toronto, gives a unique opportunity to evaluate those problems. The observations which started in 1979, showing that an average of 35 flashes per year hit the CN tower, testifies to the significance of the effect of the tower on the local climatology, and convenience of the study of the lightning characteristics. In this paper, the lightning characteristics to the tall standing structure was reviewed and compared with present tower results. The lightning current, which may be important to <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> evaluate lightning protection, will also be discussed.

articleTitle: A Simultaneous Electric and Magnetic Field Sensor for Near-Field Electromagnetic Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper describes a concept for a single sensor to perform simultaneous nearfield electric and magnetic field measurements. The theory indicates that it is possible to obtain the loop-mode and dipolemode currents using a loop terminated with identical loads at diametrically opposite points. The theory also indicates that it is possible to adjust the load impedance, and thus obtain an ideal load impedance for achieving equal electric and magnetic field responses of the loop. Preliminary experiments have been performed using plane waves to verify these results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Radiation Hazards and the Amateur Radio Service
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Work safety standards are widely used for protection against electromagnetic (EM) radiation hazards. Some countries have introduced obligatory radiation limits for general use RF power devices such as microwave ovens, citizens band (CB) radio, etc., whereas in Poland environmental standards stipulate limiting EM field intensities in residential areas. Since amateur radio stations are usually located in densely populated areas the authors have found that an investigation of the irradiation caused by these stations to the operators, their families and neigbours would be of interest. To assess the EM field levels to be expected in the vicinity of an amateur radio station some measurements were carried out for different working conditions of the transmitter (power, frequency, antenna) and their results with the corresponding conclusions are presented in the following.

articleTitle: Review of Guided Wave EMP Simulators
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The guided wave EMP simulator reviewed in this paper takes the form of a two-plate transmission line. Examples of this type of bounded wave simulators are ALECS, ARES, ATLAS I facilities at Kirtland Air Force Base in the U.S. Several European simulators also fall in this category. Much of the work that will be reviewed here is the result of research efforts during the last two decades at the Air Force Weapons Laboratory and in several universities and industries as well. The emphasis will be placed on the electromagnetic (em) charaterization of the different components of the simulator and hence, the material presented here is applicable to the general class of two- parallel plate transmission line type of EMP simulator [1].

articleTitle: Evaluation of Shielded Enclosure for EMI/EMC Measurements without and with RF Anechoic Material
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper gives the results of measurements performed by the National Bureau of Standards to evaluate the potential influence of rf absorbing material installed inside a shielded enclosure on the accuracy of EMI/EMC measurements made using the shielded enclosure. The facility evaluated was a 3.76 m wide by 6.2 m long by 2.44 m high shielded enclosure. The paper briefly discusses the measurement technique used, describes the test facility and test configurations, and the spherical dipole radiators used for generating the reference standard fields. Tests were performed to evaluate the influence of 1) placement location of both the source and receiving antenna inside the enclosure, 2) separation distance between source and receiving antenna, and 3) height of source above the floor of the enclosure on the measurement results. Measurements made before and after installation of the rf absorbing material indicated a significant improvement in accuracy (error typically less than ±10 dB as compared to >30 dB) at frequencies above 30 MHz where the absorber is effective.

articleTitle: Methods and Approaches for Studying Biological Effects of Radiofrequency Radition: AN Overview
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A large number of investigations have been conducted during the past decade for the purpose of defining (1) the effect of radiofrequency radiation biological systems and (2) the mechanisms by which this effect occurs. There has been no coordination or standardization in the methods and approaches used during these investigations, with the result being that data were obtained under a wide range of experimental designs. Thus, for instance, (1) exposure frequencies have varied from 60 Hz to approximately 10 GHz, (2) exposure power densities have varied from microwatts per square centimeter to much higher, lethal levels, (3) both pulsed- and continuous-wave fields have been used with the pulsed rates and widths varying widely for the pulsed-rate fields, (4) various exposure facility concepts have been used with each generating its own peculiar field configuration, (5) the choice of biological endpoints has varied from behavorial parameters to the collection of isolated blood components, (6) numerous animal species and/or cellular preparations have been used, etc. The result of this situation is an inability to adequately compare results from the many different investigations. This paper provides a critical overview of methods and approaches that have been frequently used in bioeffects research, with emphasis on the emerging use of chronically cannulated animals for accessing sensitive biological endpoints in animals exposed to radiofrequency radiation generated by a circular, parallel-plate facility. The overview will be specifically concerned with the areas of exposure facilities, biological endpoints, and dosimetry.

articleTitle: On the Measurement of Soil Permittivity
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The electrical parameters of the earth are a determinant of both the electromagnetic environment and the propagation characteristics of parasitic transmission channels formed byconductors in proximity to the ground. In attempts at measuring these parameters, attention has been drawn to the dominating effect of electrode polarisation. This paper develops a time dependent theory of polarisation and shows how the experimental results may be re-interpreted yielding estimates of permittivity in closer agreement with simple mixing formulae. Anomalous results for soils with low water content are explained by a further simple hypothesis, a qualitative prediction being confirmed by experiment.

articleTitle: Hemp - The UK EMP Generator of Horizontally Polarized Waves
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The historical, economical and scientific reasons behind the design of the HEMP facility are outlined, indicating the interaction of the cost, location, engineering feasibility, experimental requirements and safety. The design technique is then indicated leading to the electrical specification and finally the structural realisation. Some results of a field survey are presented showing to what extent the design requirements have been met.

articleTitle: A Practical Approach to Determine the Culling Mechanism in Electromagnetic Interference Analysis Models
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Due to the rapid growth In the number of CB radio users in Canada In the last few years, continued development of the Personal Radio Service in the 890-960 MHz frequency band Is presently being considered. One of the concerns of this development is Interference between stations and this Is similar In nature to that In the Land Mobile bands. This paper outlines some of the Land Mobile Interference analysis models [3] - [7] presently documented in open literature and describes a practical approach that can be used to determine the culling mechanism of the relatively more complexed Intermodulation Analysis model. The results of the analysis are presented on a graph depicting the relationship between the two culling limits of distance and frequency separation. This approach is then applied to the higher frequency band by using the same Interference models presently used for the UHF Land Mobile band.

articleTitle: The Effect of Repetitive Surges on Transient Overcurrent and Overvoltage Protective Devices
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The occurrence of transient overvoltages in low-voltage power circuits has been recognized, and new standards have been published in recent years [1-4] that provide quantitative information on the voltage levels to be expected. Concurrently, the technology of metal oxide varistors has gained wide acceptance in the suppression of these transients [5-7]. These varistors provide an effective method of diverting surges away from sensitive loads by offering a low-impedance path to the flow of current, maintaining a quasi-constant voltage across their terminals. This surge current diverted in the varistor produces within the bulk of the varistor material the deposition of energy, with the long-range effect of a progressive shift in the varistor characteristic. This phenomenon has been well documented [8, 9], and the proper application of varistors can deal with the effect without adverse consequences.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Cellular Mobile Communication Systems with Pseudo-Noise Signals
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: At the present tine radio communication with mobile stations is established mainly with the aid of centralised mobile communication systems (Centre MCS). In these systems a central station (CS) transmits information to and receives information from all subscriber stations installed on mobile stations (MS). The increase of the number of mobile stations provided with radiocommunication in Centre MCS presents difficulties, because, first, the number of MSs in Centre MCS can be increased at the expense of the increase of frequency channels, which is difficult to realize in practice even now; second, service area spreading leads to the increase of CS transmitter power, which in turn results in degraded EMC of Centre MCS with other systems. These difficulties can be over come by making use of cellular rather than centralized principle of communication.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Propagation Constant of Buried Insulated Conductors
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The propagation constant is one of the most important parameters for the calculation of a shielded cable response to an incident EMP wave. The aim of this work is to propose an iterative calculation method of the propagation constant of cables with an arbitrary number of layers buried in an infinite earth. Comparison of the results with calculations for single layer shielded cables using Sunde’s formulae and curves published by Head show a very good agreement. It is also shown that the use of Sunders approximative expressions, where possible, results in an important economy of computing time.

articleTitle: High Current Pulse Cable Testing System
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A current injection test facility for currents up to 15 kA is described in detail. The first measurements made with this test equipment are discussed and propositions are made to improve the accuracy. Results from a typical application, the investigation of saturable shielding materials are also presented.

articleTitle: Ariel 4 Observations of Power-Line Harmonic Radiation over North America and its Effect on the Magnetosphere
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Ariel 3 and 4 satellite studies over North America (2 < L < 4) have revealed the existence of VLF emissions above the ionosphere whose base-line intensity varies diurnally and seasonally in accord with ionospheric transmission and ground measurements of power line harmonic radiation (PLHR), The resultant wave-particle interactions (WPI) in the magnetosphere give rise to sustained and discrete emissions in the summer and winter respectively whose intensity increases with L (2 < L < 4). These stimulated emissions give rise to sustained field-aligned ducts between the North and South, assist in the formation of the Electron Slot and may be responsible for the secular increase in thunderstorm activity in Southern Canada. Line radiation events observed at Siple and Halley in Antarctica have properties (frequency, differences in overall and diurnal occurrence, line spacings) which are consistent with the nature of the WPI and longitudinal differences in PLHR intensity in the conjugate region.

articleTitle: The Conceptual Problems of Ground-Planes
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: There are difficulties in trying to express the beliefs about ground-planes and grounding systems which are commonly held by practising EMC engineers in a form which is scientifically based, and so amenable to analysis. The impact of a conventional ground-plane on the compatibility of the inter-unit wiring of a large system is held to be adverse; some pointers are developed on how to use a ground-plane to make a positive contribution to EMC.

articleTitle: Features and Potential of the AAPG Computer Code
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper describes a new computer code called Aircraft inter Antenna Propagation with Graphics· This code computes antenna- antenna coupling by means of new coupling path algorithms that are more complete than previous EMC analysis codes. It also allows the use of interactive graphics to select displays of equipment spectral analysis, aircraft models and antenna pattern displays, EMI margins and actual three dimensional displays of the coupling path· Antennas can be repositioned by a cursor and computations affected interactively. The code is written in Fortran IV, occupies 22K word of core storage on a PDP-11 mini computer and requires a Tektronix 4014 terminal.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Program for EMC Evaluation on Pipelines
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Some years ago the problem of electromagnetic compatibility between tele com lines and power lines was dealt with in Italy in a comprehensive manner in or der to develop a computer program [1], [3] able to evaluate voltages and currents induced at industrial frequencies on telecom undergroud cables: the program accuracy was verified by field tests [2] [3]. The aim of such a program was to provide a precise calculation method, for study purposes, and an easy, quick and low cost calculation method for routine purposes. As a matter of fact, the Italian geographic configuration is characterized by a few plains and many valleys and coasts which are the natural paths of communication routes as well as of power and telecom lines, which are the refore often laid close to each other. The same occurs for pipelines. For this reason SNAM, the company managing the distribution of natural gas in Italy, entrusted us with the working out of a calculation program for evaluating the effects of interference at industrial frequency on its long distance systems. Said program, called INMECA, is now available: this paper briefly illustrates its aims and its operation process.

articleTitle: A Computer Code for Magnetics Analysis of Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A computer code has been developed which will compute the magnetic dipole moment of a spacecraft, provide estimates of the field at each sensor and source (neglecting the field from the source itself) and list the ten largest contributors to the dipole moment and the fields in the vehicle.

articleTitle: A Transportable Simulation Pulser
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A high energy Marx generator has been designed and fabricated at Maxwell Laboratories, Inc., for current injection simulation. Two crucial parameters on the late-time, long-pulse injector are the high energy and high coulomb involved. With Maxwell's unique high energy density capacitor technology, a 2 MJ Marx generator has been installed in a regular 8 ft wide trailer which can be transported freely on the highways. A high coulomb rotating arc spark gap switch has been developed for this pulser. The characteristics of this pulser are: Output voltage ≈ 320 kV Internal inductance ≈8 µh; delivering a millisecond current pulse to a nominal 20 Ω load. This pulse can also drive time varying loads of from high impedance to near short circuit. Test results of the high energy capacitor, the high coulomb switch and the pulser will be presented.

articleTitle: Protection Circuits for Suppressing Surge Voltages with Edge Steepnesses up to 10 KV/NS
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Shelters, test cages and, on principle, any sensitive electronic system are shielded against electromagnetic interferences (lightning, EMP). The shielding efficiency is reduced by field coupling through apertures and by feeding of interfering currents through cable entries [1],[2]. This paper deals with the suppression of interfering currents, penetrating the shield of shelters or electronic systems via cable entries. Protection circuits for symmetrical as well as for unsymmetrical transmission lines are developed. In consideration of the application of surge voltages with edge steepnesses up to 10 kV/ns (fig. 1) a special coaxially constructed protection circuit for unsymmetrical high frequency transmission lines (characteristic impedance Z = 50 Ω)is developed. Besides a low output voltage this circuit shows a minimum 50Ω-insertion loss "a", in order to guarantee a largely non-attenuated transmission of the signals. The following results were obtained: a<0.60 dB for the frequency range 2...10 MHz, a<1.95 dB for the frequency range 2...70 MHz.

articleTitle: Increasing the RFI Immunity of Amplifiers with Negative Feedback
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Theoretical background is presented for the correct application of interference suppression capacitors in amplifiers with negative feedback. Application of the theory ensures that the wanted signal behaviour is not influenced and that the circuit remains stable. Results of experiments confirm the applicability of this theory.

articleTitle: Predicting the Long Term Effects of Environmental Stress on the Shielding Effectiveness of Conductive Coatings
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: It is not only desirable, but absolutely essential that designers of electronic equipment consider the long term effects of environmental stress on their chosen EMI/RFI shielding methods. While, at this time, no worldwide standard environmental test criteria are recognized, major efforts aimed at standardization are being undertaken on several different quarters. This presentation shows that comparative ranking of various shielding method's stability to environmental stress can be accomplished by any of several selected test criteria. By choosing an appropriate set of conditions, the EMC engineer can select an EMI/RFI shielding method which meets his product's shielding requirements now and will continue to effectively shield for the product's projected life span. Care must be taken in selecting these conditions so that the proper balance of overall cost effectiveness and assurance of product quality can be achieved.

articleTitle: Determination of the Angle of Arrival, Amplitude and Phase of Multipath Reflections
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: For many EMI/EMC problems, if the angle of arrival of an interfering signal is known, measures can be taken the decrease the system susceptibility in these directions. An example is the use of directional antennas or antennas with nulls appropriately located in the pattern. Further if the amplitude and phase of the signal are also known then other avenues are open such as the use of adaptive cancellation techniques.

articleTitle: Distributed Low-Pass Filters for EMI Filtering
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Distributed low-pass filters for EMI applications based on a combination of dielectric losses and reflections are introduced. The single-section case is presented in detail, giving characteristic filter parameters in function of geometric dimensions and typical attenuation curves showing cut-off frequencies. The latter are dampened through a proper use of dielectric losses. The attenuation slope of single-section filter is basically 20dB/decade. Practical examples illustrate the verification of the theory. The n-section case is briefly discussed; the basic principle and a few illustrative examples of measured vs. calculated curves are presented. An application example illustrates the superiority of the new, distributed filter over conventional mains filters in the VHF region.

articleTitle: ISM RFI Radiation Problem
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Radio Frequency Interference to radiocommunication services due to Industrial, Scientific, and Medical devices is considered An original model is Pro-prosed to evaluate the probability of interference and to explain the role of various factors involved. Different possibilities of protection against the interference are discussed, along with inherent difficulties.

articleTitle: The Canadian Land Mobile Interactive EMC Analysis System
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In the mid-seventies, the Department of Communications of Canada has endeavoured to develop an integrated computer-based Spectrum Management System that would support all aspects of its radio licensing activities, with a particular emphasis on computer assistance to frequency assignments in the Land-Mobile bands [l, 2, 3].

articleTitle: Overvoltage Caused by Inrush Current in HVDC Schemes
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: When transformers are energised in any circuit and in particular in power electronic or hvdc circuits the magnetising or inrush current can have an amplitude which is several times the rated current. As well as containing a fundamental component the current is very rich in harmonics and contains harmonics of all orders, both odd and even. These harmonics can exist for a considerable length of time, up to several seconds in large schemes. One of the factors which must be taken into consideration when designing harmonic filters for such a scheme is that resonance can take place between the a.c. harmonic filters and the impedance of the a.c. system which feeds the converter bus-bar. This paper describes an analytical method and the subsequent study which was carried out to determine the factors which affect the inrush current and also the overvoltages which will occur when the resonances are excited.

articleTitle: Qualification Requirements for Electronic Equipment Protected against the Electric and Magnetic Field Strengths and Peak Voltages Generated by a Nemp - A Preliminary Standard
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper introduces a preliminary standard which specifies the requirements for the verification, as part of the formal qualification, of equipment hardness against the radiated and conducted interference generated by a NEMP. It also presents the deliberations and arguments brought forward in the committee responsible for its generation, on which the actually chosen values for the qualification parameters are based.

articleTitle: EMC Design of Digital Systems using Macromodelling Procedures for Integrated Circuits and Their Interconnections.
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Computer-aided analysis is used to ensure the proper electrical functioning of the hardware of a digital system. Macromodels containing a few number of resistors, indipendent and controlled sources are used to simulate coupled interconnections and non-linearity of integrated circuits. A method for the time-domain analysis of lossy interconnections is also presented. Some simulations and measurements are compared.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Disturbances Caused by Lightning in Communication and Control Equipments
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The problem of protecting apparatus against transient overvoltages from connected transmission facilities has become more complex with the use of solid-state devices in communication control and measurement systems. In this paper an analytical method is presented to model the coupling mechanisms between a lightning discharge and transmission line. As a result, the waveshape and peak values of transient voltages induced on the ends of low-voltage overhead and buried transmission cables by lightning surge were calculated.

articleTitle: Frequency and Power Assignment to a Transmitter Network
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The paper introduces a new method of assignment which utilizes dynamic programming. The criterion of minimum overall power of the network is adopted. During the assignment process, all frequency restrictions for a given transmitter are taken into account. The method allows for fully automated assignment, making use of modern computational aids. It may be used for any number of stations.

articleTitle: Correlation of Surface Currents to Radiated Fields
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper describes a technique and measurement program to demonstrate the correlation between surface currents and radiated fields, for frequencies of 30 MHz and above.

articleTitle: The Tem-Cell in EMC Investigations
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The TEM cell is one of the oldest EMC tools used for the susceptibility investigations of material media to electromagnetic field /EME/. Simple and frequency independent relation between EMP intensity and the cell excitation as well as minimal EM energy exchange with the environment caused its wide spread applications. In the work is considered accuracy of the EMP intensity estimation in the cell loaded with an object under test /OUT/. The authors are involved in the near field EMP measurements and they use the cell mostly for EMP probes calibration. This application is here emphasized; some attention is paid, however, to other investigations eg. electric devices susceptibility measurements. The basic problem here is inseparability of the cell and the OUT. The cell changes properties of the OUT and vice versa. The OUT causes EMP distribution changes in the cell. The changes are here more important, in relation to free space, as they cause higher order modes generation and propagation in disturbed area. Disturbance makes reflections and as a result of this difficulties with the cell excitation measurement. The cell influes upon the EMP energy absorption by the OUT due to changes of the OUT input impedance in the cell.

articleTitle: Urban MF Radio Noise Survey in Poland
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The paper reviews the investigation of the composite man-made noise performed in 124 Polish cities ranging in size from 1 to 600 thousand inhabitants. Theoretical models and experimental results have been presented.

articleTitle: New Views on the Absorbing Clamp in the Testing of Cable Screening Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The screening effectiveness may be measured with the absorbing clamp (RF-current probe) in a simple and fast way, but the absolute calibration of a given test site was more laborious up to now. We model the test site as an inhomogeneous transmission line (travelling wave monopole) and obtain by known theories a good physical insight into the measurement and calibration procedure; further we are able to predict test site characteristics with closed form expressions with excellent accuracy. From these findings we deduce a simple calibration procedure. The reproducibility between various test sites and cables is satisfactory. In addition we give the relations between screening effectiveness and complex transfer immitance values.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experimental Study of Switching and Ignition Interference in Motor Vehicles
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper deals with the noise produced by the mechanical switching and gap breakdown. A brief view is made on discharge as a noise source, and some wave observations are made. The APD's are measured of the induced noise due to an inductive load circuit switching in the cases where circuit voltage, current and inductance are changed respectively. Finally, some theoretical and experimental studies are shown on the frequency spectrum of the noise by using sophisticated model systems.

articleTitle: Application of Computers for the Determination of Magnetic and Electromagnetic Coupling
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Electronic data processing has proved to be practically indispensable for planning and analysis of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). The paper describes the foundations and applications of three computer programs for the determination of magnetic and electromagnetic coupling. The first program mentioned calculates the magnetic flux density of arbitrarily oriented electrodes under the assumption that the current flowing is known. By use of the second program the mutual inductance between arbitrary loops, defined by the edge points, can be determined. It will be shown that a cable shield current is produced by a symmetrical current in a twisted wire. The third program based on the method of moments will be applied to show the interactions between two thin wire aerials close to each other in simultaneous operation. In a final example the electrical field strengths delivered by the computer program will be compared with the values obtained by approximate calculations.

articleTitle: Radiated Emissions from Transmission Lines in Digital Control Systems
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: An efficient numerical method of examining the effects of typical on-board vehicular digital signal transmission structure parameter variations on far field radiation of harmonics in the reception bands of sensitive on-board receivers is presented. The numerical model is based on obtaining approximate current distributions using classical transmission line theory; comparisons to the more exact solutions obtained by moment method analysis are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: EMI Control in Power Distribution
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Different disturbances measured in the last years in electrical distribution networks have been analysed. The present work presents a classification on families of disturbances based on three parameters - the place (swiss supply networks), the time (1978 to 1982) and the coupling mode (transmission of disturbances trough galvanic mode (R), inductance or mutual inductance mode (L,M) or capacitance mode (C)) (1). Most of the measured disturbances can be classified in 4 categories based on a frequency criteria: voltage fluctuations and dips, voltage or current harmonics, micro-disconnections and over-voltages (2).

articleTitle: The Shielding Effectiveness of Long Cables, III: Maximum Leakage
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In our laboratory, many cable shield leakage measurements have been made, all of which show that for a given length of cable, as frequency is increased, a maximum occurs in the shield leakage· This leakage maximum is never exceeded as frequency is further increased. These experimental observations are confirmed theoretically by examining the equation describing the coupling of energy through the shield·

articleTitle: Environment Compatibility Model for Search Radar Deployment
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A modeling approach is developed for predicting the electromagnetic compatibility of a specified radar at a selected site. The approach, requiring only the basic characteristics of the radar and its electromagnetic environment, utilizes an accepted performance criterion as the basis for assessing the EMC of the prospective radar installation. The algorithm can also be applied to selection of a compatible frequency for the additional system or for identifying frequency reassignments to achieve electromagnetic compatibility.

articleTitle: The Rationale for Radio Frequency Electromagnetic Exposure Standards
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: It has been universally recognized for many years that living organisms are affected by exposure to radio frequency electromagnetic fields (RFEM). In order to permit the orderly development of the technology associated with the generation, propagation and utilization of RFEM fields without harmful effects to those so involved and in fact on the environment in which we live, it is necessary to understand how living organisms, and especially humans, interact with RFEM fields and to establish a basis for permitting work with these fields to be continued without associated hazards to all who may be exposed or in contact with such fields.

articleTitle: Instrumentation for EMP Measurements
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: EMP assessments of complex systems require that hundreds or even thousands of test points be monitored for induced transients, mostly of currents on internal wires. An instrumentation system has been developed which greatly accelerates the data acquisition process by allowing $$ erates the data acquisition process by allowing $$ then switching to new sets of test points remotely, without requiring access to the test object. A single such instrumentation system allows for up to sixty-four such test points to be measured with a minimum of time and test shots, usually within a single day of testing. Reconfiguration to a new set of test points can then be performed during non-testing periods of the day. The instrumentation system also includes the isolated data links to bring the data out of the test environment, the probes which made the measurements, and various signal conditioning devices. A computerized control and processing system is included which provides both for control of the data acquisition system and for data manipulation and storage. Control of the EMP pulser and simulator can also be provided by this automated system, making the entire data acquisition process fully automated.

articleTitle: Loop Antenna Hear a Boundary Plane
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Circular loop antenna placed near a "boundary plane is analysed; Por this antenna the integral equation for current distribution is formulated and solved with the Pourier-series-expansion method.

articleTitle: Some Considerations about Interference Voltage Measurements and Relevant Limits
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The problem of radio interference voltage measurement is dealt with critically considering artificial mains networks and methods recommended by CISPR. Taking into account how modern radio-receivers for LW and MW are actually interfered, improvements in present procedures are proposed together with new limits. Particularly, the connection between effective interfering magnetic field and interference voltage measured at the mains cord of portable tools and household appliances is considered.

articleTitle: A Computational Technique for the Design of Absorber-Lined Chambers
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The prediction of field structure in ALC's by a G.O. based computational technique is described as a design tool. The effects of shape, dimensions and absorber properties are investigated.

articleTitle: The Effect of Terminations on Coupling to Wires and Pairs
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Simple, controlled experiments were used to demonstrate the effects of various shield terminations on the effectiveness of the shield in preventing external sources from interacting with internal circuits. The configurations tested included a short wire (pigtail) connection between the cable shield and the terminal enclosure, a closed peripheral connection to a grounded terminal enclosure, and a floating cable shield. For these experiments, RG-62 coaxial cable terminated in matched loads was used for the shielded cable, and the current in the matched load was measured with a current probe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> If interference is induced as a commonmode current, balanced twisted pairs are effective in rejecting the common-mode interference while transmitting the differential mode signal. However, if unbalanced terminations are used, part of the common-mode current will be converted into differential current at the terminations. Experiments were performed with twisted shielded pairs for various shield terminations and load imbalances to demonstrate both shielding and imbalance effects. For both the coaxial cable and the shielded twisted pair, the measurements were conducted in a frequency range from 100 kHz to 50 MHz to demonstrate the low-frequency effects where pigtail inductance is negligible and the high-frequency effects where pigtail and aperture effects are Important. Among the conclusions are: (1) the closed shield affords almost 80 dB more protection than the floating shield, and (2) the balanced termination can provide as much as 80 dB more commonmode rejection than the unbalanced termination.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Coupling to Telecommunication Networks
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper presents an experimental and theoretical Investigation of the behavior of overhead telecommunication cables exposed to electromagnetic fields. We give experimental results obtained in an electromagnetic simulator: shield current, common and differential mode voltages at the end of the cables, cable shielding discontinuity effect. In addition a campaign of automatic measurement is in hand to record surges (dc to 5 MHz) gathered from telecommunication lines spread across the country. After the description of this project we give the initial results.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Discharge Diagnostics and Control
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: be the coupling culprit. An inspection often shows that I/O and RS-232 cables act as an antenna farm. Until they are properly screened and or filtered, ESD failures can occur at levels of 1 kV or lower, rather than a mission objective of perhaps 15 kV Finally, the paper addresses the subject of the ESD diagnostic methodology and procedures as applied to equipment in its R&D or development stage. One significant problem here is the need to simulate the geometrical setup and I/O interconnected cables often found in real- life installations. Otherwise ESD failure levels would yield results which are far too optimistic.

articleTitle: The Compatibility of Standards
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: It is not so very long ago that it was very difficult if not impossible for some manufacturers to export to many countries because national governments levied tariffs and fixed quotas on imports.
