Progress has been made in the sense that various GATT arrangements (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) have virtually eliminated tariff as a barrier to trade, this being augmented in the European Community by actions arising from the Treaty of Rome. As the tariff barriers have disappeared the prospective exporter has run up against another set of obstacles which are technical in nature and are known as technical barriers to trade. It is the task of national governments and the international standardization bodies to remove the obstacles arising from differing technical requirements and practices in different parts of the world.

articleTitle: Shield, a Digital Computer Program for the Prediction of Crosstalk to Shielded Cables
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A digital computer program tor the prediction of electromagnetic coupling between shielded cables which may have pigtails is described. Experimental data showing the prediction accuracy of the program are also given. The program is written in Fortran IV language and should be usable on a wide variety of digital computers.

articleTitle: Use of a Monopole Antenna for EMI Measurements
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The problems associated with measuring vertically polarized fields over a ground plane in the 30 to 1000 MHz frequency range are examined. Fall-off, cable coupling, and nonuniform illumination errors are identified by comparing measured and calculated vertical site attenuation. Both monopole and dipole receive antennas are included. The limitations of using a monopole to perform EMI measurements are also discussed.

articleTitle: New Directions for EMC Standards
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Whereas it is possible to carry on a multitude of useful EMC activities, as far as some institutions can afford them, it is not possible to manage EMC without standards. A critical review of existing EMC documents and their guiding principles is presented· In order to overcome existing limitations new directions are explored. There has been increasing demand for EMC during, the last 20 years or so, but the supply of standards has been disproportionately low· The main reason for the delay is that in the EMC field there are no clear lines of responsibility or authority which are required for rational management. A Common Policy and a Document Standard may ease some of these difficulties. One set of international methodology standards for electrical/ electronic equipment which is common to all sectors would be the most effective achievement of priority. Economic, industrial and political conflicts which concern mainly the issue of limits are manageable by a flexible categorization process. A paradoxical aspect of EMC standards is that the more we strive for accuracy, the further we move away from the target.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Radiation Hazards to Ordnance and Personnel by Computerized Simulation
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Hazards of EM Radiation to Ordnance Program (HEROP), is an interactive computer program (Fortran IV) which analyzes the effects of EM Radiation to Ordnance and produces hardening recommendations as follows: a) Minimum Recommended safety Distance (MRD) between ordnance and intentional radiation sources; b) MRD for electronic equipment, due to its RF vulnerability or susceptibility; c) Recommended wiring of EED firing circuits to meet the safety margin required (e.g. 20 dB above susceptibility level) in a given EM Environment (EME); and d) EM Shielding required for electronic equipment in a given EME due to its susceptibility and the safety margin required. In addition, analysis is performed to estimate the safety margin for an EED subjected to conducted interference. The advantage of the computer program outlined in this article is in offering the user a worst-case estimation of "HERO" with a minimum knowledge of ordnance parameters and by tailoring an actual EM Environment constructed on a very simple computerized data-base.

articleTitle: AC - Harmonic Filters for Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The harmonic currents required by static power converters can cause excessive voltage distortion on ac power systems. The proper design and application of power sized filters can trap the harmonic currents and provide improved power factor of the load. The paper has an example of how effective different filtering arrangements are, It also shows before and after wave forms of corrected voltage waves.

articleTitle: Coupling to Transmission Lines: An Overview
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper presents the author's view of the status of modeling transmission lines for the purposes of predicting unintentional electromagnetic coupling (crosstalk) or the pickup of an incident electromagnetic field by transmission lines. A general discussion of the modeling of ideal lines is given. Discussions of the modeling of nonideal line perturbations as well as other practical variations from the ideal are also given.

articleTitle: High Voltage EMP Pulse Generator
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper describes the design, construction and test of a pulsed high-voltage system capable of generating a horizontally polarized EMP. The pulser contains a pair of trigger 1 MV, 6.6 nF Marxes charged to opposite polarities. When erected, each Marx simultaneously charges a peaking capacitor in 75 ns. Then, a self-firing output switch closes which connects the two Marx/peaking circuits in series and discharges them into a horizontally polarized, 150 Ω biconic antenna. The output pulse has a 2 MV peak amplitude and a 500 ns e-fold decay time. The 10-90 percent risetime is <4 ns. Amplitude reproducibility is <3 percent and jitter (1σ) is <5 ns. The pulser is triggered through fiber-optic trigger links. Pulser voltage is monitored with a separate fiber-optic data system with response time in the nanosecond range. The trigger and data links are 450 m long. The pulser command and control are accomplished through pneumatic links, also 450 m long. The fiber-optics and pneumatics allow remote ground-based operation of the system while the pulser is attached to an elevated antenna structure.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Coupling to Balanced, Twisted Pair Lines to Line Twist
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The sensitivity of crosstalk between an interfering circuit and a balanced, twisted pair circuit due to variations in line twist is examined. It is found that the crosstalk can change by as much as 40dB when one end of the twisted pair is rotated slightly (no more than 180°).

articleTitle: Threshold Detection in Non-Gaussian Interference Environments: Exposition and Interpretation of New Results for EMC Applications
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The critical problem of developing optimum weak-signal detection algorithms for general classes of man-made and natural interference is concisely examined. This includes a summary of new results for both canonical and specific types of desired signals and electromagnetic interference (EMI) environments. A suitable bias term, missing in most earlier analyses, is essential to preserve the asymptotically optimum (AO) character of these algorithms, as sample-size (or observation period ∼ n) necessarily becomes large, to enable the detection of weak signals with acceptably small probabilities of error. Canonical optimum threshold algorithms are obtained for three principal modes of detection: (1), coherent; (2), incoherent; and (3), composite. The latter (3) is AO, also, when it consists of the sum of (optimum) algorithms for (1) and (2), and can give noticeable improvement over either (1) or (2) alone. Various (usually) suboptimum algorithms, e.g., simple correlators and clipper correlators, are also considered. Performance measures (n>>l), e.g., error probabilities, etc., and asymptotic relative efficiencies (ARE's) are noted, along with the useful concepts of processing gain and minimum detectable signal. Interpretations of the algorithmic structure and the implications of these results, generally, for EMC, are concisely discussed.

articleTitle: Advances in Experimental Exposure Methods and Dosimetric Techniques Used in Radiofrequency Bioeffects Studies
publicationTitle: 5th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The various techniques and methodologies used for exposure and dosimetric assessment in radiofrequency (RF) bioeffects studies are reviewed. Techniques are compared and the advantages and disadvantages of each are discussed. Significant progress has been made during the past decade in developing the specialized techniques required; suggestions are givin for further studies.
